messages.subject: Precision for model hyperparameters
parts:
Hi,

I'm running a model that is defined like this:

> formula<-Y~f(Id, model="iid")
> model = inla(formula, family="binomial", control.compute = list(dic=T,cpo=TRUE),data=datos,Ntrials=N)

I would like to know which is the difference between the Precision of the model hyperparameters that shows up on the result window and the marginals hyperparameters that you could obtain once the model is been run, using this sintaxis:
> tau.Eta<-model$marginals.hyperpar$`Precision for Id`
> 
> m1<-inla.expectation(function(x) (1/x^.5), tau.Eta)
> m2<-inla.expectation(function(x) (1/x^.5)^2, tau.Eta)
> sd<-(m2-m1^2)^.5
> print(c(mean=m1,sd=sd))


Thank you very much!

Ariadna.

messages.author: afb003e064114795
messages.subject: Re: Precision for model hyperparameters
parts:
Hi!

Can you please clarify your question?

"Precision for Id" refers to this being the precision parameter of the f(Id, ...) effects in your model.
What you are calculating seems to be the posterior mean and standard deviation for the standard deviation of f(Id, ...) ?

/Finn
